s: Fixed 57 failing frontend test files (109 cases) surfaced after the Next14 migration, restoring a trustworthy CI test suite.
pr: After migrating to Next14 (and from Jest to Vitest), 57 of 519 test files (109 test cases) were failing due to pre-existing component/test logic issues such as missing context providers, style-assertion mismatches, and async/mock configuration problems — not the migration itself.
wy: A reliable, passing test suite is required to safely ship and refactor the frontend; failing tests undermine CI confidence.
oc: Failing tests across auth, comments, documents, events, filters, lead capture, mixed cards, and meeting program components were fixed by adding missing context providers, correcting style assertions, and fixing async/mock handling.

s: Introduced a net-new V3 endpoint to retrieve event sponsors with full profile, category and placement data, broadening the public API's coverage for partner integrations.
pr: There was no V3 endpoint exposing sponsor data with profile, category and visibility/placement flags for programmatic retrieval.
wy: Future Proofing / integration capability - expose sponsor data via the modern V3 API.
oc: A new GET /api/v3/events/{eventId}/sponsors endpoint was delivered returning sponsor profile, category and placement configuration with pagination.

s: Fixed disabled database cleanup that let stale records pile up across test runs and inflate counts in 3 test suites.
pr: With database cleanup disabled in functional.suite.yml, DataFactory-created records persisted across runs, inflating counts in EventsReadRepositoryCest, DeleteBasketItemCest, and ActualTicketsCest.
wy: Explicitly classified as a test-environment issue, not application logic.
oc: Restoring database cleanup between test runs is expected to eliminate cross-test data leakage.

s: A tenant-by-tenant audit of category-data completeness gives a go/no-go signal on whether AI Agenda Builder's matching logic has enough signal to work.
pr: AI Agenda Builder's matching logic relies on interest categories being set on both exhibitors/sessions and registered visitors, but no one had measured how complete that data actually is across live tenants.
wy: A data-quality audit is needed before committing to a recommendation design, since poor category coverage would starve the matching algorithm regardless of its quality.
oc: A tenant-by-tenant completeness audit of category assignment on exhibitors/sessions and registered visitors, checking taxonomy consistency, delivered as a short summary with a go/no-go recommendation for AI Agenda Builder feasibility.

s: Automatically removing deleted users from the Meeting Program keeps the matchmaking and scheduling data clean so meetings are not booked against accounts that no longer exist.
pr: When users were deleted, they remained referenced in the Meeting Program, leaving stale participants that could break scheduling and matchmaking integrity.
wy: Platform Health / Maintenance — stale deleted-user references caused data-integrity problems in the meeting workflow.
oc: Deleted users are now stripped from the Meeting Program, so only valid participants appear in matchmaking and meeting data.

s: A standing time-tracking practice has the team log synchronous meeting time monthly, giving leadership visibility into meeting overhead across the team.
pr: There was no measurement of how much time the team spent in meetings and calls, so meeting overhead was invisible to management.
wy: Internal Efficiency — leadership wanted quantified visibility into meeting time to manage overhead.
oc: A monthly per-person meeting-time logging convention was set up (one sub-task per person per month) to capture synchronous meeting/call time; work is ongoing.

s: Catalogued all API endpoints used for Exhibitor CRUD to ground the upcoming Exhibitor CRUD module build.
pr: Before building or refactoring exhibitor CRUD functionality, the team lacked a documented inventory of which endpoints perform create, read, update and delete on exhibitors.
wy: Necessary discovery step to de-risk and scope the "Implement Exhibitor CRUD" epic.
oc: A list of Exhibitor CRUD endpoints annotated by action type (Create/Read/Update/Delete) was produced.

s: Completed systematic QA of the public Open API v2 endpoint /api/v2/exhibitor/get, hardening exhibitor data exposed to external integration partners so the published API behaves reliably and to spec.
pr: The Open API v2 endpoint /api/v2/exhibitor/get had not been formally quality-assured, so defects, contract mismatches or edge-case failures could surface for external partners consuming exhibitor data, with no logged baseline of its behaviour.
wy: Prioritised under the API V2 Quality Assurance initiative (Platform Health / internal quality drive) to certify each Open API endpoint before partners rely on it, rather than in response to a specific customer request.
oc: The /api/v2/exhibitor/get endpoint was exercised end-to-end, any defects found were logged as individual linked bugs and resolved, and the endpoint passed QA and shipped to production (Prod release), giving a verified, documented baseline for exhibitor data.

s: Switched translations to load dynamically in next14, reducing what needs to be bundled upfront.
pr: Translations were likely bundled statically, which is inefficient for the next14 architecture.
wy: Reduces bundle size and improves performance by loading translations on demand.
oc: Translations now load dynamically in next14.
